ai.literal: Self-control among the immortals will lead; lack of self-control into deep darkness having led will leave.
ai.translation: Self-control will lead one to the realm of the immortals, while the lack of self-control will lead and plunge one into deep darkness.
ai.modern: அடக்கம் ஒருவரைத் தேவர்களுள் கொண்டு சேர்க்கும்; அடக்கமில்லாமை அவரைப் பேரிருளில் கொண்டு சேர்த்துவிடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet contrasts the ultimate destinations of self-control and the lack of it. The word 'அடக்கம்' (self-control) is shown as an active force that elevates a person to the level of 'அமரர்' (immortals or highly respected beings). Conversely, 'அடங்காமை' (the absence of restraint) drags a person down into 'ஆரிருள்' (deep, dense darkness), symbolizing ignorance, misery, and ruin. The poet uses the verb root 'உய்' (to lead or direct) in both lines to emphasize that our inner discipline actively guides our destiny.

ai.literal: Let one guard self-control as a treasure; prosperity greater than that there is not for life.
ai.translation: One should guard self-control as a precious treasure; there is no greater wealth than that for a person's life.
ai.modern: அடக்கத்தை ஒரு சிறந்த செல்வமாகக் கருதி அதைக் காக்க வேண்டும்; மனித உயிருக்கு அதைவிடச் சிறந்த செல்வம் வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of self-control. The poet advises us to protect and nurture self-restraint (அடக்கம்) as if it were our most precious wealth (பொருள்). The second line reinforces this by stating that there is absolutely no greater source of true prosperity or elevation (ஆக்கம்) for a human life (உயிர்) than possessing this single virtue.

ai.literal: Knowing the value of self-control, greatness it will yield, if, knowing wisdom, one is able to remain restrained in that path.
ai.translation: If one acquires wisdom and remains self-controlled in that path, that restraint, being recognized, will bring them great excellence.
ai.modern: அறிய வேண்டியவற்றை அறிந்து, நல்வழியில் அடங்கி வாழப் பெற்றால், அந்த அடக்கமானது அவனுக்குப் பெருமையைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights how self-control leads to true greatness when guided by wisdom. The poet states that if a person acquires proper knowledge and uses it to walk in the path of self-restraint, that restraint itself becomes a source of great dignity. The word 'cerivu' refers to the firmness of self-control, which yields excellence when practiced knowingly. Thus, true self-control is not passive, but an active, wise choice of conducting oneself in the right path.

ai.literal: From his proper state without deviating, he who is self-controlled, his moral stature, even than a mountain, greatly, is great.
ai.translation: The moral stature of one who remains self-controlled without deviating from his proper path is far greater than even a mountain.
ai.modern: தன் நன்னெறியிலிருந்து மாறாமல் அடக்கத்தோடு வாழ்பவனுடைய உயர்வு, மலையின் அளவை விடவும் மிக மிகப் பெரியதாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the immense value of self-control. The poet compares the moral stature of a person who stays true to their righteous path and practices self-restraint to a mountain. While a mountain is physically massive, the spiritual and moral greatness of a self-controlled person is described as being far greater. The word 'தோற்றம்' here refers to one's true dignity or moral stature, and 'நிலையின் திரியாது' emphasizes consistency in one's ethical position.

ai.literal: To everyone, good it is, humility; among them, to the wealthy indeed, wealth's quality it has.
ai.translation: Humility is good for everyone; yet, among them, for the wealthy, it is a wealth that possesses the true nature of wealth.
ai.modern: பணிவுடன் நடப்பது எல்லாருக்கும் நல்லது. ஆனால், அவர்களுள் செல்வந்தர்களுக்கு அந்தப் பணிவே மேலும் ஒரு செல்வமாக விளங்கும் தகைமையைப் பெற்றுள்ளது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the universal value of humility (பணிதல்) while emphasizing its special beauty in those who are prosperous. While being humble is a virtue that benefits anyone, it becomes an extraordinary ornament for the rich (செல்வர்). For those who already possess material abundance, practicing humility is considered a supreme wealth in itself (செல்வம் தகைத்து), as it is rare and commands the highest respect.

ai.literal: Within one birth, like a turtle, if one is able to restrain the five, it has protection throughout seven births.
ai.translation: If a person can restrain their five senses in a single birth like a turtle withdrawing its limbs, that self-control will serve as a protective shield throughout all seven of their future births.
ai.modern: ஒரு பிறவியில் ஆமை தன் ஐந்து உறுப்புகளையும் அடக்குவது போல ஒருவன் தன் ஐந்து புலன்களையும் அடக்கிக் காக்க வல்லவனானால், அது அவனுக்கு ஏழு பிறவிகளிலும் பாதுகாப்பாக அமையும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares self-control to a turtle withdrawing its five limbs into its shell for safety. If a person can master and restrain their five senses within a single lifetime, this discipline becomes an enduring strength. The poet asserts that the protective power of such self-control is not temporary; it safeguards the individual across all future births. The key words 'ஐந்தடக்கல்' (restraining the five senses) and 'ஏமாப்பு' (protection/shield) emphasize that self-discipline is the ultimate armor for the soul.

ai.literal: Whatever they do not guard, even if, the tongue they should guard; if they do not guard it, they will suffer, having fallen into a slip of the tongue.
ai.translation: Whatever else one fails to guard, one must guard the tongue; if one fails to guard it, one will suffer, trapped by the slip of one's own words.
ai.modern: எவற்றைக் காக்கத் தவறினாலும் நாவையாவது காக்க வேண்டும்; அவ்வாறு காக்காவிட்டால், சொற்குற்றத்தில் சிக்கித் துன்பப்படுவர்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the supreme importance of self-control in speech within the chapter on self-restraint. The author states that even if a person is unable to control other senses or aspects of their life, they must at all costs control their tongue. If they fail to do so, they will inevitably utter harmful or erroneous words. This slip of the tongue will lead to deep regret and suffering, as spoken words cannot be recalled and their consequences are lasting.

ai.literal: Even if one evil word's harmful consequence arises, goodness will end up becoming non-existent.
ai.translation: If even a single evil word spoken causes harmful consequences, all the other good done by a person will become completely ruined.
ai.modern: பேசும் சொற்களில் ஒன்றே ஒன்று தீய சொல்லாக இருந்து, அதனால் தீய விளைவு ஏற்பட்டால், ஒருவருடைய மற்ற நன்மைகள் அனைத்தும் பயனில்லாமல் போய்விடும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet emphasizes the extreme caution needed in speech as part of self-control. The author warns that even if a person has practiced great virtue and done much good, a single slip of the tongue that causes harm (தீச்சொல் பொருட்பயன்) can completely destroy the merit of all those good deeds. The phrase 'poruṭpayaṉ' refers to the actual harmful consequence or sting carried by the meaning of the word. Therefore, self-restraint must be absolute, as even a single lapse in speech can undo a lifetime of goodness.

ai.literal: A wound burnt by fire will heal on the inside; but the scar burnt by the tongue will never heal.
ai.translation: A wound caused by fire will heal on the inside, but the scar left by a burning tongue will never heal.
ai.modern: தீயினால் ஏற்பட்ட காயம் உள்ளே ஆறிவிடும்; ஆனால் நாவினால் ஏற்பட்ட வடு எப்போதும் ஆறாது.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the lasting damage of harsh words compared to physical injuries. A physical wound caused by fire may be painful, but over time, the body heals it from within. However, a wound inflicted by the tongue—cruel, bitter, or insulting words—leaves a deep psychological scar (வடு) that remains fresh in the mind and never truly heals. The poet uses the metaphor of 'burning' (சுட்ட) for both fire and the tongue to emphasize that words can burn just as intensely as physical fire, but with far more permanent consequences.

ai.literal: Anger guarding, having learned, self-restraint he who is able to practice, his opportunity, Virtue will look for, by the path, having entered.
ai.translation: Virtue itself will seek out the opportunity to enter the path of one who has learned to control his anger and practice self-restraint.
ai.modern: கோபத்தைக் கட்டுப்படுத்தி, நல்லவற்றைக் கற்று, அடக்கத்தோடு வாழ்பவனுடைய நல்வாய்ப்பை, அறமானது அவனது வழியிலே நுழைந்து தேடிப் பார்க்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the supreme value of self-restraint combined with anger management and learning. For a person who achieves this level of self-control, Virtue does not wait to be sought; rather, Virtue itself actively seeks out the right opportunity to enter their life's path and bless them. The word 'கதம்' means anger, and 'காத்து' means guarding or restraining it. 'செவ்வி' refers to the opportune moment or favorable time, showing that righteousness waits for the perfect moment to reward the self-controlled individual.
